Effect of electrical impedance tomography-guided positive end-expiratory pressure optimisation on postoperative pulmonary complications in laparoscopic colorectal surgery: a randomised controlled trial. Pneumoperitoneum and steep Trendelenburg positioning during laparoscopic colorectal surgery promote atelectasis and increase the risk of postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs). Electrical impedance tomography (EIT) enables individualised PEEP titration by visualising regional lung collapse, facilitating lung-protective ventilation. However, evidence of its effect on clinical PPCs remains limited.

Amplification of interferon-γ-driven proinflammatory macrophage responses by granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor: Implications for colorectal cancer immunotherapy. Tumor-associated macrophages in colorectal cancer predominantly exhibit an immunosuppressive M2 phenotype that contributes to tumor progression and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibition. Repolarizing M2 macrophages toward a proinflammatory M1 phenotype represents a promising immunotherapeutic strategy. While interferon-γ promotes M1 macrophage activation, the effect of combining interferon-γ with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor remains underexplored.

Clinical Outcomes of Bladder-sparing Management Versus Early Radical Cystectomy in cT1 Micropapillary Bladder Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Clinical T1 micropapillary urothelial carcinoma of the bladder is an aggressive variant histology for which early radical cystectomy (RC) is commonly recommended. However, there remain conflicting data on whether conditions in carefully selected patients may be managed with initial bladder-sparing approaches without compromising oncologic outcomes.
